subtype_info: Pancoast syndrome and Horner's syndrome due to pulmonary apical and vertebral hydatid cyst
title: Pancaost syndrome related to hydatid cyst
case_text:
This 38 year old immunocompetent man coming from a rural area was followed in our department for vertebral hydatid cyst disease for 4 years. He had been operated twice for thoracic and lumbar hydatid cyst revealed by recurrent paraplegia. He complained of a two month history of cervical and shoulder pain radiating downward toward the ulnar side of his left arm and forearm reaching the fourth and fifth fingers. Physical examination revealed decreased muscular strength in the fingers mainly in the last fingers of the left hand associated with thenar and hypothenar muscle atrophy (Figure 1). Horner's syndrome of the left eye, namely a miosis, ptosis and enophtalmos with ipsilateral facial anhidrosis was also noticeable.
Radiological examination consisting of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a multi vesicular lesion of the left pulmonary apex which was hypointense on T1 weighted images. This lesion was hyperintense on T2 weighted images and delineated by a hypointense rim with a "bunch of grapefruit" appearance (Figure 2). There was also an invasion of the first and second thoracic vertebrae as well as the corresponding ribs. Serologic test results for hydatid cyst were positive. The patient was operated with the assistance of thoracic surgeons through a left Paulson thoracotomy. Post operative period was uneventful and adjuvant Albendazole based chemotherapy was administrated.

   - Never extrapolate findings not explicitly mentioned.

2. THE ADMISSION BREAKPOINT PRINCIPLE (CRITICAL):
   - The <case_prompt> represents what an emergency triage clinician knows on Day 1 BEFORE confirmatory tests return.
   - INCLUDE in <case_prompt>: Demographics, travel/occupational/vector exposures (freshwater contact, insect bites, animal exposure), symptom chronology, vital signs, physical exam findings, and initial triage laboratory/imaging results (CBC, platelets, basic metabolic panel, LFTs, urinalysis, plain chest radiograph, bedside ultrasound).
   - STRICTLY EXCLUDE from <case_prompt>:
     * Any mention of the disease name or pathogen genus/species (e.g., do not write "Leptospirosis", "Burkholderia", "Leishmania", "Paragonimus").
     * Confirmatory send-out PCR panels, serological titers, blood culture organism identifications, or biopsy histopathology.
     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Echinococcosis
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: Pancoast syndrome and Horner's syndrome due to pulmonary apical and vertebral hydatid cyst
